title: Filtered two-colimit presentation of condensed Qbar bounded constructible complexes
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, write $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and order its finite intermediate extensions $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ by inclusion [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Use the condensed rings $\underline E(S)=C(S,E)$ on profinite sets and the coefficient pullback $p_T^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. Define $\underline\Omega(S)$ to be the subring of $C(S,\Omega)$ consisting of continuous functions whose values lie in one finite intermediate extension, with restrictions by precomposition. Thus $\underline\Omega$ is the archived $\mathrm{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell)$, not the full continuous-function sheaf. Put $E_T^c=p_T^*\underline E$ and $\Omega_T^c=p_T^*\underline\Omega$. Write $\mathcal C_E^c(T)$ for the bounded constructible module-object category of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], and define $\mathcal C_\Omega^c(T)$ by the identical construction with coefficient ring $\Omega_T^c$: a full subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Omega_T^c})$, with bounded cohomology, each cohomology sheaf stratified pro-etale locally finitely presented. No derived completeness condition is imposed. Let $T_{E,F}^T=F_T^c\otimes^L_{E_T^c}-$ and $T_{E,\Omega}^T=\Omega_T^c\otimes^L_{E_T^c}-$ denote derived extension of scalars along the coefficient inclusions. Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying space is noetherian (every ascending chain of open subsets stabilizes). These scalar extensions preserve the displayed bounded constructible categories and have the canonical tensor-transitivity comparisons. The cocone with vertex $\mathcal C_\Omega^c(T)$ is a filtered two-colimit: its comparison functor sends $(E,K_E)$ to $T_{E,\Omega}^T K_E$ and is an equivalence. Here the source pair category has objects $(E,K_E)$ with $K_E\in\mathcal C_E^c(T)$ and morphisms represented by maps $T_{E,H}^T K_E\to T_{F,H}^T L_F$ at finite $H\supseteq E,F$, modulo equality after further scalar extension, with composition at a common finite overfield using tensor associativity. Explicitly, every object of $\mathcal C_\Omega^c(T)$ is isomorphic to some $T_{E,\Omega}^T K_E$; every morphism between two such objects descends to a common finite overfield; and two finite-stage morphisms with equal images become equal after a further finite extension. These finite-stage categories are condensed module-object categories, not the raw rationalizations of integral categories.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], the rings $C(S,E)$ form a directed union equal to $\underline\Omega(S)$ by its definition. This union is a sheaf: for a finite jointly surjective family of profinite sets, choose the compositum of the finitely many fields containing the matching sections; these sections glue in $C(-,E)$ at that common field. Compatible maps from the $\underline E$ to any abelian sheaf therefore define a unique sheaf map from this union, by assigning to each section its value at any containing field. This proves the colimit universal property in abelian sheaves (and in ring sheaves for ring maps). The geometric inverse image $p_T^*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] is a left adjoint, so its image is the colimit $\Omega_T^c=\varinjlim_E E_T^c$. The same union and universal property hold over the fields containing any fixed finite $E$, since every finite field is contained in its compositum with $E$.

proof.text: Work in the larger universe of [def-weil-size-convention], so the poset of finite overfields and the pro-etale site skeleton are small. The finite fields are nonempty and directed by compositum [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Use the coefficient colimit established in the preceding elementary step. The exactness and termwise derived tensor computations of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus] give $H^q(T_{E,B}K)=B_T^c\otimes_{E_T^c}H^q(K)$ for $B=F,\Omega$. On every stratum, tensoring a finite presentation $E^m\to E^n\to M\to0$ gives $B^m\to B^n\to B\otimes_E M\to0$. Thus these functors preserve precisely the stated bounded constructible categories. Their comparisons are tensor multiplication; on a pure tensor $g\otimes(f\otimes k)$ each composite sends it to $gf\otimes k$, and the unit sends $1\otimes k$ to $k$. The coherence and shift comparisons in the calculus node therefore restrict to these full subcategories.

proof.text: First prove the Hom comparison for a single constructible sheaf $M$ over a fixed finite $E$ and a bounded below complex $L$. By [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], represent $L$ by a complex zero in degrees below some $a$, and put $N_H^\bullet=U_{H/E}(H_T^c\otimes_{E_T^c} L^\bullet)$ for finite $H\supseteq E$. The flat coefficient calculus identifies these termwise complexes with the derived extensions, all with the same lower bound, and identifies their termwise colimit with $U_{\Omega/E}(\Omega_T^c\otimes_{E_T^c}L^\bullet)$. The sheaf continuity node applied to $M$ and $(N_H^\bullet)$ is therefore applicable, and its bijection followed on both sides by the tensor-restriction adjunction gives $$\varinjlim_{H\supseteq E}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(H_T^c)}(T_{E,H}M[0],T_{E,H}L[n])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\Omega_T^c)}(T_{E,\Omega}M[0],T_{E,\Omega}L[n]).$$ Naturality of the continuity map and adjunction says this is exactly the map sending a finite-stage arrow to its scalar extension, with the comparisons of step 2; it is not an unrelated bijection of groups.

Extend the comparison of step 3 to every bounded constructible first argument $K$ by induction on a finite cohomological interval $[a,b]$ containing $K$. The zero case has zero Hom groups. For the induction step use the truncation triangle $A=\tau_{\leq b-1}K\to K\to M=H^b(K)[-b]\to A[1]$ of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]. Its endpoints are bounded constructible by the definition of cohomology, and step 3 applies to every shift of $M$. Exact scalar extension sends this triangle to distinguished triangles. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] and its rotations to obtain the five-term rows $$\operatorname{Hom}(A,L[n-1])\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,L[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,L[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,L[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,L[n+1]).$$ Their filtered colimit is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. The comparison diagram commutes: its arrows are precomposition with the triangle arrows, and tensor functors preserve composition and the shifted boundary. The induction hypothesis and step 3 make the four outer vertical maps bijective, so [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] makes the middle map bijective, for every $n$. This proves the full bounded-complex Hom comparison inside the parent, rather than assuming its Hom clauses as a new node.

proof.text: Before descending objects, check cones at finite and algebraically closed coefficients. By [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], for a triangle $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ the sheaf $H^q(C)$ is an extension of $\operatorname{coker}(H^q(A)\to H^q(B))$ by $\ker(H^{q+1}(A)\to H^{q+1}(B))$. If $A,B$ are bounded constructible, the Serre closure node makes both pieces and their extension constructible. The same exact sequence shows vanishing outside the union of the two finite cohomological intervals, with one endpoint shifted by one. Shifts preserve the condition by reindexing cohomology. Thus any cone or rotated cone used below is still in the actual condensed bounded constructible category.

Let $K$ over $\Omega_T^c$ have cohomology in $[a,b]$. Induct on $q$ to descend $\tau_{\leq q}K$. For $q<a$ choose the zero object over the base field. Suppose $A=\tau_{\leq q-1}K$ has been descended over $E$; descend the single constructible sheaf $H^q(K)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-finite-presentation-descent], and enlarge to a compositum so both descended objects $A_E$ and $M_E=H^q(K)_E[-q]$ are over $E$. Their scalar extensions are still bounded constructible by step 2. In the truncation triangle $A\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to H^q(K)[-q]\xrightarrow{\delta}A[1]$, conjugate $\delta$ by the two chosen descent isomorphisms. Step 4 with shifted target $A_E[1]$ gives a finite $H\supseteq E$ and an arrow $\delta_H:T_{E,H}M_E\to T_{E,H}A_E[1]$ whose scalar extension is that conjugate. Complete $-\delta_H$ to a cone triangle and inverse-rotate (TR2), so its last arrow is $\delta_H$: the middle object is $B_H=\operatorname{Cone}(-\delta_H)[-1]$ in a triangle $T_{E,H}A_E\to B_H\to T_{E,H}M_E\to T_{E,H}A_E[1]$. Step 5 makes $B_H$ bounded constructible. Step 2 carries this to a triangle over $\Omega$ with boundary $\delta$. TR3 applied to the rotated triangles extends the endpoint isomorphisms; Hom exactness and the five lemma show the third arrow is an isomorphism (test Hom from every object), hence $T_{H,\Omega}B_H\cong\tau_{\leq q}K$. This completes the induction. At $q=b$ the truncation is $K$ since its higher cohomology vanishes, proving object descent without assuming compatibility of unexamined differentials.

For objects over different $E,F$, first extend both to the compositum $E_0=EF$. Step 4 with $n=0$ identifies the colimit of their Hom groups over $H\supseteq E_0$ with the desired Hom group over $\Omega$. By the elementwise filtered-colimit node every arrow there has a representative at some $H$, proving Hom-surjectivity. If two arrows have equal images, move their representatives to a common finite stage; injectivity of the comparison of step 4 and the same elementwise node imply their equality after one further extension, proving Hom-injectivity. This applies also to shifted targets. Only the condensed categories defined in this item are involved.

Construct the pair category directly as stated here. A representative $u$ at $H$ is transported to $P\supseteq H$ by the tensor-transitivity comparison on its source and target. Eventual equality is reflexive and symmetric; transitivity follows by moving two equality witnesses to their compositum. Define composition by transporting two representatives to a common field and composing there. Replacing either representative or the common field gives the same class, because tensor is a functor and its coherent associators identify successive transports. Associativity and the identity law are then checked at one common field using ordinary categorical composition. The comparison to $\mathcal C_\Omega^c(T)$ is well-defined for exactly the same reason: the cocone comparisons satisfy the unit and pentagon identities of step 2. Step 7 makes it fully faithful and step 6 makes it essentially surjective. Choose a preimage and an isomorphism for each object, and lift each conjugated arrow uniquely by full faithfulness; this defines a quasi-inverse and its two natural isomorphisms. Hence the comparison is an equivalence, giving the filtered two-colimit claim. No integral rationalized pair category is invoked.
